0xd822.name: wBriefingSwingFrame
0xd822.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: swing-animation frame (0-9); indexes BriefingSwingAnimTable0 for the base tile, and < 6 selects the 5-sprite racket template

0xd823.name: wBriefingVMarkerX
0xd823.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: vertical marker X, queued by DrawBriefingMarkerVFlip

0xd825.name: wBriefingVMarkerUpright
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the vertical marker upright (OAM attr $09), anything else Y-flipped ($49)

0xd826.name: wBriefingSpinMarkerUnflipped
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the spin-serve marker unflipped (OAM attr $09), anything else X-flipped ($29)

0xd827.name: wBriefingRotMarkerDir
0xd827.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: rotatable marker orientation (0-3); indexes BriefingMarkerRotatedTable, the four flip combinations of OAM attr $x9

0xd828.name: wBriefingBracketX
0xd828.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket top-left X; DrawBriefingTargetBrackets draws the four corners at X, X+width+3

0xd829.name: wBriefingBracketY
0xd829.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket top-left Y; corners sit at Y and Y+height-5

0xd82a.name: wBriefingBracketWidth
0xd82a.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket width in pixels (corner offset is width+3)

0xd82b.name: wBriefingBracketHeight
0xd82b.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket height in pixels (corner offset is height-5)

0xd82c.name: wBriefingAnimTimer
0xd82c.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing animation frame timer; each briefing's *_TickAnim increments it and calls *_AdvanceAnim at $78 (120 frames)

0xd82d.name: wBriefingHMarkerUnflipped
0xd82d.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the horizontal marker unflipped (OAM attr $09), anything else X-flipped ($29)

0xd82e.name: wBriefingAnimStep
0xd82e.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing animation step; each briefing's *_AdvanceAnim wraps it (and a & $03) and indexes its 4-byte-per-step position table with it

0xd830.name: wBriefingTargetPalette
0xd830.note: [8 bytes] Drill-briefing target palette scratch: CycleDiagramTargetPaletteData copied here, colour 2 ($d834) replaced with the cycling colour, then uploaded by LoadPaletteShadow

0xd811.name: wCharGridPage
0xd811.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: top row currently shown (wMenuCursorX/Y address the cell within it); MoveCharGridCursor* wrap it and rebuild the page sprite list

0xd812.name: wCharGridPageCount
0xd812.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: number of pages, looked up from wCharGridEntryCount through CharGridPageCountTable

0xd813.name: wCharSelectMode
0xd813.note: [8-bit] Character-select mode id stored on entry by RunExhibitionCharSelectScreen / RunLinkCharSelectScreen; picks the slot-box table and the starting slot (3 and 5 start at slot 2)

0xd814.name: wCharSelectSlot
0xd814.note: [8-bit] Character-select: player slot being chosen (0-3); $04 means every slot is filled and the screen shows the wait banner

0xd815.name: wCharSelectExitCode
0xd815.note: [8-bit] Character-select result polled by the frame loop: 0 keep running, 1 finished, 2 cancelled out

0xd816.name: wCharSelectSlotChars
0xd816.note: [4 bytes] Character id chosen for each player slot ($ff = empty); ResolveSelectedCharIds and InitMatchCharsFromSelection read it. Bank $10's CopyExhibitionCharSlotIds copies all four out to wMatchSlotCharRefs once the screen is done, which is the only reference to this block from outside bank $38

0xd81a.name: wCharGridEntryCount
0xd81a.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: roster entries present from $da24 on (CountCharGridEntries)

0xd81b.name: wCharGridPrevPage
0xd81b.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: page saved when a left/right wrap jumps to the roster pages

0xd81c.name: wCharGridBuilt
0xd81c.note: [8-bit] Set to 1 by BuildCharGridFromUnlockFlags once the grid has been populated

0xd81d.name: wCharSelectRemoteSlot
0xd81d.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: slot the remote player is choosing; Advance/RetreatRemotePlayerSlot step it

0xd81f.name: wCharSelectRemoteChars
0xd81f.note: [2 bytes] Link character-select: character ids the remote player has locked in (slots 2 and 3)

0xd821.name: wLinkSelectCmdChar
0xd821.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: character id carried by the last received select command

0xd822.name: wLinkSelectSlotState
0xd822.note: [8-bit] Link character-select slot bookkeeping, reset when a selection is retreated

0xd823.name: wCharGridCreatedCount
0xd823.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: entries present in the nine created-character rows at $da00 (counted alongside wCharGridEntryCount)

0xd824.name: wCpuDifficultyPrompt
0xd824.note: [8-bit] Set when the slot just filled needs the CPU-difficulty submenu; the frame loop runs RunCpuDifficultySubmenu instead of normal input while it is set

0xd825.name: wCpuDifficultyPanelOpen
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Set once OpenCpuDifficultyPanel has drawn the panel, so the submenu only opens it on the first pass

0xd826.name: wCpuDifficultyCursor
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Cursor value in the CPU-difficulty submenu; stored into wCharSelectSlotDifficulty on confirm

0xd830.name: wCharSelectSlotDifficulty
0xd830.note: [4 bytes] CPU difficulty chosen per player slot; ApplyCpuDifficultyToCharRecords copies it into the match character records

0xd834.name: wCharSelectSlotLeftHanded
0xd834.note: [4 bytes] Left-handed flag per player slot, toggled with START on the character grid (only the nine Mario-cast characters may be toggled). ApplyHandednessToCharRecords copies it to the four match records' +$0e, which LoadCharacterAttributes turns into wCharMirrorAttrMask -- the OAM X-flip plus the forehand/backhand swap in SelectForehandBackhand

0xd838.name: wLinkSelectCmdResult
0xd838.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: result byte ProcessLinkSelectCommand leaves for commands $24-$27

0xd839.name: wLinkCpuDifficulty
0xd839.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: CPU difficulty for the link match, stepped by HandleLinkCpuDifficultyInput

0xd820.name: wWindowId
0xd820.note: [8-bit] Window struct index AllocWindowStruct handed out for the window being built, $ff when none was free; CreateMenuWindowFromText passes it to SetWindowTextId / SetWindowState and returns it

0xd824.name: wDialogueWindowId
0xd824.note: [8-bit] Window struct index of the dialogue window currently on screen, stored by CreateDialogueWindow. RedrawActiveTextWindow, RenderActiveWindowText, CloseActiveDialogueWindow and the speaker-dialogue helpers all address the window through it

0xd825.name: wDialogueWindowCol
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window top-left tilemap column (wrapped to $1f)

0xd826.name: wDialogueWindowRow
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window top-left tilemap row (wrapped to $1f)

0xd827.name: wDialogueWindowHeight
0xd827.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window height in cells, from b at CreateDialogueWindow

0xd828.name: wDialogueWindowWidth
0xd828.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window width in cells, from c at CreateDialogueWindow

0xd829.name: wTextRedrawGuard
0xd829.note: [8-bit] Re-entrancy guard around RedrawActiveTextWindow: the delay/wait text commands only redraw while it is 0, and set it for the duration of their own redraw

0xd82f.name: wMenuWindowId
0xd82f.note: [8-bit] Window struct index of the menu window CreateMenuWindowFromText just built (a copy of wWindowId taken as the menu is pushed)

0xd830.name: wMenuCursorRow
0xd830.note: [8-bit] Row the menu cursor sits on; RunMenuSelection steps it against wMenuRowCount and returns it as the chosen entry

0xd831.name: wMenuRowCount
0xd831.note: [8-bit] Number of selectable rows in the current menu, derived from MeasureTextDimensions ((lines - 1) / 2)

0xd832.name: wMenuStack
0xd832.note: [12 bytes] Six two-byte frames, one per nested menu, indexed by wMenuDepth * 2: [wMenuRowCount << 4 | saved wMenuCursorRow, window id]. Pushed by CreateMenuWindowFromText and unwound when a menu is cancelled

0xd83e.name: wMenuDepth
0xd83e.note: [8-bit] Number of menus currently stacked; indexes wMenuStack

0xd821.name: wGlyphWindowId
0xd821.note: [8-bit] Window struct index the glyph stream is rendering into, set by RedrawWindowText / RenderWindowTextToCompletion. InitGlyphStreamForWindow, DrawWindowGlyphRun, FlushGlyphRow and UploadLastGlyphTiles all resolve the window through it

0xd82a.name: wTextCursorColumn
0xd82a.note: [8-bit] Column of the text-drawing cursor, 0-31. RenderTextString seeds it from d masked to $1f alongside wTextCursorRow, and TextCmdNewline reloads it into d for the GetTilemapCellAddress call that re-points the write pointer -- d is the column there, e the row (the row counter is what steps hl by $0020).

0xd82b.name: wTextCursorRow
0xd82b.note: [8-bit] Row of the text-drawing cursor, 0-31. TextCmdNewline advances it by *two* rows, not one, because the font is double height; it wraps with `and $1f`. The two glyph-stream row commands at $5425/$544f compare it against a row computed from the stream offset to decide whether to step.

0xd822.name: wGlyphBufferHoldCount
0xd822.note: [8-bit] While nonzero the glyph buffer survives: PrepareGlyphBuffer only calls ClearGlyphBuffer and ResetGlyphStream when it reads 0, and DrawTileAttrRect decrements it as it tears a window down. No site in bank $05 ever increments it, so whatever raises the count does so from another engine's variant of this byte.

0xd810.name: wEquipItemCount
0xd810.note: [8-bit] Number of entries BuildOwnedItemList put in wEquipItemList

0xd811.name: wEquipEquippedIndex
0xd811.note: [8-bit] Index within wEquipItemList of the item currently equipped (the slot BuildOwnedItemList saw marked 2)

0xd812.name: wEquipSelectExitTimer
0xd812.note: [8-bit] 0 while the screen is running; once a choice is made it counts up each frame and the screen fades out at $14

0xd813.name: wEquipItemKind
0xd813.note: [8-bit] 0 = rackets, 1 = shoes; selects the icon set, the info panel and which stat-modifier table GetItemStatModListPtr reads

0xd814.name: wEquipStatRowSet
0xd814.note: [8-bit] Which row-address table GetStatModRowAddr uses for the stat-modifier panel; both loaders set it to 0

0xd810.name: wStatsPrintBuffer
0xd810.note: [8 bytes] Digit scratch PrintSinglesMatchStats / PrintDoublesMatchStats hand to PrintNumberRightAligned as bc while writing each stat into the shadow tilemap

0xd812.name: wMinigameDataStarFlags
0xd812.note: [9 bytes] One byte per list row, nonzero when that row's minigame has its level-2 clear flag. LoadMinigameStarFlags fills it from MinigameStarFlagsTable ($02a0/$0300/$0360/$03c0/$0520/$0580/$05e0/$0640/$06a0, the SAVEFLAG_CLEARED_*_2 run) exactly as wMinigameDataClearFlags is filled from the level-1 flags. DrawMinigameStarMarks draws mark 1 for each set row; DrawStarLegendMark copies the legend swatch onto the screen if any of the nine is set; and DrawMinigameHighScoreNumber returns early unless the row's byte here is set, so a row with no star shows no number

0xd81b.name: wMinigameDataHighScores
0xd81b.note: [8 x 16-bit] The number shown on each of the first eight rows. LoadMinigameHighScores calls ReadMinigameRecord with the record id row + 2 -- records 2-9 of the block $38 minigame records, whose 16-bit value comes back in wMinigameRecordValue under WRAM bank $07 -- and stores it at row * 2. DrawMinigameHighScoreNumber skips row 8, which has no record: that slot holds wMinigameDataTwoOnOneCleared instead

0xd82b.name: wMinigameDataTwoOnOneCleared
0xd82b.note: [2 bytes] Row 8's slot in the high-score array, used as a flag pair rather than a number: LoadMinigameHighScores writes $01 into both bytes when SAVEFLAG_CLEARED_TWO_ON_ONE_3 is set, having cleared all 18 bytes from $d81b first. DrawMinigameSpecialMark reads the pair as a word and, once the list is scrolled to the bottom (wMenuCursorY = 4, so row 8 is the fifth visible row), draws mark 2 there

0xd812.name: wTrophyCellsPartnerSet2
0xd812.note: [6 bytes] The partner's second-set trophy row, from wN64TrophyCounts + 1 bits 2-3 and 6-7; the fourth and last row DrawTrophiesWonRows draws, and only when wTrophySecondSetPresent

0xd819.name: wTrophySecondSetPresent
0xd819.note: [8-bit] Set by DecodeTrophyCounts when any of the four second-set counts came out nonzero. It picks screen asset record $0d over $0e and switches DrawTrophiesWonRows and the character sprites from two rows (main at tilemap row 8, partner at 10) to four (rows 6/8 and 13/15)

unions.comment:
Character-data (level-up) screen working set, WRAM bank $06, shared by
the bank $1a/$1c/$1d screen code. The first four bytes are a smaller
scratch that three screens overlay -- the debug character viewer, the
results continue prompt and the character-data screen itself -- so those
get their own range-scoped variants ahead of it.
Every scope carries wram_bank $06. The viewer and the continue prompt both
started with ROM-range-only scopes and both were naming other banks' bytes
at $d000 -- the results screen's tilemap planes, the viewer's actors --
which the scope audit found once traced banks made the sites provable.

0xd000.name: wStarWarpFrame
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Animation frame of the warp star, 0-5, stepped every other VBlank by UpdateStarWarpSprite

0xd001.name: wStarWarpPathIndex
0xd001.note: [8-bit] How far the star has travelled along its path, stepped by two each frame. OffsetStarWarpPathPoint indexes StarWarpPathY and StarWarpPathX with it to get the point wStarWarpPathX/Y then carry

0xd002.name: wStarWarpCountdown
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Frames left in the transition, seeded to $5a. The wait loop starts the fade out when it reaches $1e and returns at zero

0xd003.name: wStarWarpSparkleLife
0xd003.note: [16 bytes] One life counter per trail sparkle. UpdateStarWarpTrailSparkles finds the first zero, sets it to $10 and seeds that slot's position from wStarWarpPathX/Y; the positions themselves are two bytes per slot from $d014

0xd004.name: wCharViewerPalette
0xd004.note: [8-bit] Palette index the debug character viewer is showing, from GetCharPaletteIndex

0xd005.name: wCharViewerPose
0xd005.note: [8-bit] Animation/pose index the debug character viewer is showing, stepped by RunCharViewerInputLoop

0xd000.name: wCharViewerRow
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Which row of the debug character viewer the cursor is on, toggled with `xor $01`: 0 = the character grid, 1 = the palette row

0xd001.name: wCharViewerCursor
0xd001.note: [8-bit] Cursor index within the current row; up/down step it by $0b, the grid width

0xd002.name: wCharViewerCharId
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Character the viewer is showing, chosen by RunCharViewerSelectGrid and turned into wCharViewerPalette by GetCharPaletteIndex

0xd003.name: wCharViewerSavedCursor
0xd003.note: [8-bit] Grid cursor saved while the palette row has focus, so switching rows comes back to the same character

scopes.note: InitExpAwardScreenState sets wContinuePromptKind to 1 before ShowExpAwardScreen calls InitResultsScreenCharacters, which is inside the range above and reads the byte at $49fa to decide whether to check FLAG_TEMP_RESULTS_SCREEN_OPEN. Same variable, written from outside the prompt's own code.

0xd000.name: wContinuePromptKind
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Which continue prompt is up, stored from c by InitResultsPromptState

0xd001.name: wContinuePromptRow
0xd001.note: [8-bit] Cursor row, toggled 0/1 by up and down; picks which of the two cursor sprites DrawContinuePromptCursor queues

0xd002.name: wContinuePromptPage
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Which page of the prompt text is showing (RefreshContinuePromptText)

0xd003.name: wContinuePromptResult
0xd003.note: [8-bit] What the prompt returned: 1 confirm, $ff cancel, or wContinuePromptPage - 1

0xd000.name: wCharDataAnimCounter
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Free-running counter CharDataScreenAnimTask steps every frame the screen is idle; its low nibble indexes the animation table

0xd001.name: wCharDataAnimSubStep
0xd001.note: [8-bit] Cleared alongside wCharDataAnimCounter when the screen opens. Nothing in banks $1a/$1c/$1d reads it back -- the byte belongs to whichever screen ran before

0xd002.name: wCharDataFlushChunk
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Which third of the screen still needs pushing to VRAM. FlushCharDataTilemapChunk sends one chunk per call and branches on 0, 1 and 2; while it is nonzero the animation task holds off

0xd003.name: wCharDataPointsWorking
0xd003.note: [8-bit] Points still unspent while the player is editing. It heads the six bytes BackupCharData copies out and RestoreCharData copies back -- this byte, wCharDataLevel and the four wCharDataNewLevels -- which together are everything a cancelled visit has to forget

0xd004.name: wCharDataLevel
0xd004.note: [8-bit] Level the character-data screen is committing; WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer stores it back into record +$18 (wStoryModeMainCharacterLevel)

0xd005.name: wCharDataNewLevels
0xd005.note: [4 bytes] Spin/Power/Control/Speed levels the screen is committing; WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer stores them back into record +$38-$3b

0xd009.name: wCharDataPointsLeft
0xd009.note: [8-bit] Unspent level-up points on the character-data screen, copied in from $d003 and decremented by CharDataScreen_InputLoop after each LevelUpPlayer

0xd00a.name: wCharDataLevels
0xd00a.note: [4 bytes] Spin/Power/Control/Speed levels as loaded from record +$38-$3b (LoadCharStats / LoadCharStatsWithLevelUpDeltas)

0xd00e.name: wCharDataStats
0xd00e.note: [11 bytes] The eleven displayed stats, loaded from record +$20-$2a with 1 added to each (Top, Slice, Serve, Stroke, Volley, Angle, Placement, Speed, Dash, Reaction, Stop -- the order of wStoryModeMainCharacterTopStat onwards)

0xd019.name: wCharDataStatDeltas
0xd019.note: [11 bytes] Per-stat change the pending level-up would apply, filled by ComputeLevelUpStatDeltas (or cleared when wCharDataPage is $04); DrawStatArrowIndicators turns each into an up/down arrow beside its stat

0xd024.name: wCharDataPage
0xd024.note: [8-bit] Which of the four level-up choices the cursor is on, or $04 for the confirm cell; CharDataScreen_DrawPageColumns and DrawStatValueSprites both key off it

0xd025.name: wCharDataConfirmState
0xd025.note: [8-bit] Step of the confirm prompt (RunCharDataConfirmScreen); DrawCharDataPromptCursor draws the cursor from it

0xd026.name: wCharDataRevealTimer
0xd026.note: [8-bit] AnimateCharDataStatsReveal countdown between stat rows; CharDataScreen_InitState seeds it with $0a

0xd027.name: wCharDataRevealStep
0xd027.note: [8-bit] AnimateCharDataStatsReveal step; CharDataScreen_InitState seeds it with $03

0xd028.name: wCharDataLevelPreview
0xd028.note: [8-bit] 0 while the allocation page is live: DrawStatValueSprites then draws the level one higher, in palette $0f, to preview the level about to be gained. CharDataScreen_InitState sets it to $03 on re-entry and CharDataScreen_Show clears it

0xd029.name: wCharDataChoiceCount
0xd029.note: [8-bit] Number of entries written to wCharDataChoiceLog so far; also the write index

0xd004.name: wExpAwardScreenState
0xd004.note: [8-bit] First byte of the EXP award screen's working set. InitExpAwardScreenState clears $d004-$d027 from here -- wExpAwardRunningTotal, wExpAwardAmount, wExpAwardIndex and wExpAwardMessageTimer all fall inside -- then seeds $d009-$d00c and $d019-$d01c to $20 and $d00d/$d01d to $30. Nothing in bank $1e reads the byte itself; only the address is used, as the base of that clear

0xd005.name: wExpAwardRunningTotal
0xd005.note: [16-bit] The EXP total ticking up on screen. CountUpExpTotal increments it and decrements the amount still to add, one point and one sound per pass, and DrawExpTotalDigits redraws it

0xd007.name: wExpAwardAmount
0xd007.note: [16-bit] The award being counted in, set as each message is shown

0xd024.name: wExpAwardIndex
0xd024.note: [8-bit] Which award message is being shown; BeginNextExpAward steps it and DrawNextExpAwardMessage returns zero once the list runs out

0xd026.name: wExpAwardMessageTimer
0xd026.note: [8-bit] Cleared as each award begins, so the message holds for its full dwell

0xd001.name: wCutsceneTextScrollRows
0xd001.note: [8-bit] First byte of the current TextPageDescriptors_03 entry: how many rows the page scrolls by. ScrollCutsceneTextWindow masks it to two bits and treats zero as one, so a descriptor that forgets the field still scrolls a single row

0xd028.name: wTrophyExpGroup0
0xd028.note: [16-bit] EXP for trophy group 0. It is the head of the six-word run ComputeTrophyExpAwards fills, but it falls below the union wTrophyExpByGroup is filed under, so groups 1-5 carry that name and this one stands alone

unions.comment:
WRAM bank $06 from $d02a up, shared by four subsystems that never run at
once. The palette fade engine's two 128-byte buffers straddle what used
to be the boundary between two unions, which is why they are one now.
Every scope carries a ROM bank and wram_bank $06: the working palette
buffer and the character-data screen's stat arrays start at the same
address, and only the owning bank tells them apart.
The sound driver's scope keeps its wram_bank $07 alternative, since the
same offsets are its channel state in that bank.

0xd040.name: wStarWarpPathX
0xd040.note: [8-bit] X of the point the star has reached along its path, copied into each sparkle as it spawns

0xd02a.name: wTrophyExpByGroup
0xd02a.note: [10 bytes] EXP for trophy groups 1-5, five 16-bit words. ComputeTrophyExpAwards fills them one group at a time carrying a running sum in hl -- group 0's word goes two bytes lower still, onto the byte the character-data screen calls wCharDataLevelPreview, which is why the array cannot be declared from its true base here

0xd034.name: wTrophyExpGroupAccum
0xd034.note: [16-bit] ComputeTrophyExpForGroup's own accumulator while it walks one group's trophies, testing and setting each award flag as it goes

0xd036.name: wTrophyExpTotal
0xd036.note: [16-bit] The sum of all six groups, which ApplyPendingExpAwards adds to the match award

0xd038.name: wTrophyExpGroup
0xd038.note: [8-bit] Character group being totalled; indexes TrophyExpForGroupTable0-4 and selects the row GetTrophyExpValue reads

0xd02a.name: wCharDataChoiceLog
0xd02a.note: [100 bytes] One byte per level-up taken on this visit: the wCharDataPage the player confirmed. Cleared by WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer before the screen opens

0xd08e.name: wCharDataNumberBuffer
0xd08e.note: [6 bytes] Scratch the character-data and EXP screens format numbers into. FormatExp24BitDecimal puts the 24-bit value's top byte at +$00 and formats the low word to five places from +$01, which is what makes the buffer six wide

0xd09f.name: wCharDataRevealDone
0xd09f.note: [8-bit] Cleared with the rest of the screen state by CharDataScreen_InitState and read by nothing else in the character-data banks -- the byte sits between wCharDataNumberBuffer and the working palette buffer, so whichever screen ran before is what left a value in it

0xd0a0.name: wCharDataStatsNoRacket
0xd0a0.note: [11 bytes] The eleven stats recomputed as if no racket were equipped, so the screen can show what the equipment is worth. CharDataScreen_BuildStats fills it from wStoryMainCharStats after RecomputeStatsWithoutRacket, and leaves it alone when nothing is equipped

0xd0ab.name: wCharDataRacketDeltas
0xd0ab.note: [11 bytes] Per-stat difference the equipped racket makes, cleared to zero before anything else so an unequipped character shows no arrows at all. DrawStatChangeArrows reads it alongside wCharDataStatsNoRacket

0xd0b6.name: wCharDataViewOnly
0xd0b6.note: [8-bit] Nonzero opens the character-data screen read-only: CharDataScreen_Show skips the allocation flow, LoadCharStatsWithLevelUpDeltas returns without computing deltas, and the input loop will not spend a point. Set by RunExpDistributionFlow and RestoreCharData

0xd0b7.name: wCharDataEditBackup
0xd0b7.note: [6 bytes] Copy of wCharDataEditState taken as the screen opens; RestoreCharData copies it back and sets wCharDataViewOnly, which is how cancelling out of a level-up returns everything unspent

0xd0bd.name: wCharDataChoiceBackup
0xd0bd.note: [101 bytes] The matching backup of wCharDataChoiceCount and the choice log behind it, so a cancelled visit forgets every level-up the player had provisionally taken

0xd100.name: wSndChannels
0xd100.note: [192 bytes] Six 32-byte channel state blocks (channels 0-1 music, 2-5 SFX); the active channel's block is mirrored into HRAM $ffd0 each pass, first word = script pointer ($ffff = idle)

0xd1c0.name: wSndLoopSlots
0xd1c0.note: [72 bytes] Per-channel loop bookkeeping (counter + return pointer per loop level); base resolved by GetChannelLoopSlot

0xd208.name: wSndActiveMask
0xd208.note: [8-bit] Bitmask of channels already serviced/keyed this update pass (AbortIfChannelTriggered tests it; folded into rAUDTERM at the end)

0xd209.name: wSndPanShadow
0xd209.note: [8-bit] Shadow of rAUDTERM: per-channel left/right output enable bits accumulated across channels

0xd20b.name: wSndChannelBits
0xd20b.note: [8-bit] Current channel's stereo output bit-pair (ch1=$11 .. ch4=$88), used for active-channel tracking

0xd20c.name: wSndChannelPanMask
0xd20c.note: [8-bit] Same bit-pair as wSndChannelBits, masked against hSndPanMask to build wSndPanShadow

0xd20d.name: wSndRegBase
0xd20d.note: [8-bit] Current channel's APU register offset (type*5); WriteChannelReg forms rAUD via $ff10+this+reg

0xd20e.name: wSndFrameCounter
0xd20e.note: [8-bit] Free-running update counter; low nibble supplies the vibrato phase in TickVibrato

0xd20f.name: wSndChannelIndex
0xd20f.note: [8-bit] Index (0-5) of the channel currently being updated

0xd212.name: wSndUpdateReqMask
0xd212.note: [8-bit] Pending channel-update request: mask of channels to reconfigure (SetChannelUpdateRequest)

0xd213.name: wSndUpdateReqData
0xd213.note: [8-bit] Value applied by the pending channel-update request (low nibble)

0xd214.name: wSndUpdateReqAck
0xd214.note: [8-bit] Accumulator of channels that have acknowledged the pending update request

0xd215.name: wSndFirstChannel
0xd215.note: [8-bit] Channel index the update pass starts from (normally 0)

0xd217.name: wSndLoadedWaveId
0xd217.note: [8-bit] Wave-pattern id currently loaded into wave RAM (change detection for the wave channel)

0xd218.name: wSndTranspose
0xd218.note: [8-bit] Global transpose added to note ids (cmd $a9 $fe/$f2/$f3)

0xd219.name: wSndWaveReloadPending
0xd219.note: [8-bit] Non-zero to force the wave channel to reload its pattern on the next note

0xd145.name: wCharDataStatsSlideX
0xd145.note: [16-bit] X offset the stat digits are drawn at while a page slides. The Slide*StatPage routines step it and DrawCharStatDigitsTask hands it to ApplySlideOffsetToSpriteX for every digit it queues

0xd147.name: wCharDataValuesSlideX
0xd147.note: [16-bit] The same offset for the value column, stepped in step with wCharDataStatsSlideX and applied by CharDataValuesSyncTask -- two offsets because the two columns slide in and out at different times

0xd161.name: wExpScreenCharStats
0xd161.note: [2 x 15 bytes] Per-character record the EXP award screen works on, selected by wStoryCharacterSlot (slot 0 at +0, slot 1 at +15). InitExpScreenCharStats fills $d161-$d16f; +8 is the 16-bit total CheckExpLevelUp/Down compare, and DrawExpScreenLevelNumber, DrawExpScreenLevelBar and the SweepExpBarMarker routines read +0 and +3

0xd0a0.name: wWorkingPalettes
0xd0a0.note: [128 bytes] The palettes being faded: 16 palettes of four 16-bit colours. BackupMasterPalettes seeds it from wMasterPalettes, ClearWorkingPaletteBuffer zeroes all 64 colours and DesaturateWorkingPalettes rewrites each one through SplitColorComponents. AdvanceToPaletteEntry walks it 8 bytes at a time

0xd140.name: wMasterPalettesBackup
0xd140.note: [128 bytes] The untouched copy taken at the same moment, so a fade always has its endpoint to interpolate from and can be snapped back

0xd1e0.name: wPaletteFadeMask
0xd1e0.note: [8 bytes] One flag per palette, set from the bits of b at SetupPaletteFadeMask -- bit 7 is palette 0. Only flagged palettes are stepped

0xd1f0.name: wPaletteFadeAmount
0xd1f0.note: [8-bit] How far through the fade, as passed in d

0xd1f1.name: wPaletteFadeIndex
0xd1f1.note: [8-bit] Palette currently being stepped, saved across the AdvanceToPaletteEntry calls that resolve the same entry in both buffers

0xd1f2.name: wPaletteColorSplit
0xd1f2.note: [6 bytes] The two colours being interpolated, unpacked to red, green and blue by SplitColorComponents -- the working colour at +$00 and the target at +$03

0xd1f9.name: wPaletteFadeStep
0xd1f9.note: [8-bit] wPaletteFadeAmount divided by $1f, the per-component step the fade moves each call

0xd1fe.name: wCutsceneWindowSliding
0xd1fe.note: [8-bit] Set while a cutscene text window is sliding, by AnimateWindowSlideUpTask and the scrolling-story player

0xd142.name: wCharDataPageArrowMode
0xd142.note: [8-bit] Which page arrows to bob: 1 draws the left one, 2 the right, 0 neither. DrawCharDataPageArrowsTask reads it every frame

0xd143.name: wCharDataArrowHold
0xd143.note: [8-bit] Nonzero freezes the arrow bob; while it is clear the task steps wCharDataArrowPhase

0xd144.name: wCharDataArrowPhase
0xd144.note: [8-bit] Free-running counter the arrow bob reads for its offset

0xd122.name: wCharStatPageMain
0xd122.note: [13 bytes] The main character's stat page as it will be drawn: +$00 the four Spin/Power/Control/Speed levels copied out of wCharDataLevels, +$04 six values the page copies to wCharStatPageShown, +$0a three more the value sync task reads

0xd12f.name: wCharStatPagePartner
0xd12f.note: [13 bytes] The partner's page, same layout 13 bytes on -- which is what makes the two a pair rather than two unrelated blocks

0xd13c.name: wCharStatPageShown
0xd13c.note: [6 bytes] Whichever page is on screen, copied from +$04 of the main or partner record as the screen slides between them. DrawCharStatDigitsTask draws from here

0xd149.name: wCharDataSyncSource
0xd149.note: [8-bit] Which pair CharDataValuesSyncTask pushes into the screen: zero takes wCharDataSyncValues, nonzero takes wGameTimer + 2

0xd14c.name: wCharDataSyncPair
0xd14c.note: [2 bytes] The two bytes it copied in, formatted and drawn as the screen's live readout

0xd14e.name: wExpPoolRemaining
0xd14e.note: [16-bit] EXP points still to hand out. AssignExpPointToChar decrements it per point spent, DrawExpPoolReadout prints it and DrawExpPoolGauge draws it as a fraction of wExpPoolTotal

0xd150.name: wExpPoolTotal
0xd150.note: [16-bit] What the pool started at, kept so the gauge has a denominator. Both are seeded from hl by InitLevelUpScreenState

0xd17f.name: wExpCursorChar
0xd17f.note: [8-bit] Which character the distribution cursor is on; cleared when the screen opens

0xd180.name: wExpCursorSlide
0xd180.note: [8-bit] Slide progress for the cursor moving between characters, stepped by SlideExpCursorToMainCharTask

0xd181.name: wExpBarMarkerX
0xd181.note: [8-bit] X of the marker sweeping along the EXP bar. $a8 is its home; SweepExpBarMarkerLeft subtracts the per-frame step and snaps back to $a8 once it passes $18

0xd182.name: wExpPromptCursorRow
0xd182.note: [8-bit] Row the confirm prompt cursor sits on

0xd183.name: wExpRepeatDelay
0xd183.note: [8-bit] Frames before a held direction starts repeating, seeded to $08 when the screen opens

0xd184.name: wExpRedrawPending
0xd184.note: [8-bit] Set when something changed and the screen needs its tilemap rows pushed again

0xd185.name: wExpInputRepeating
0xd185.note: [8-bit] Set once a held direction has begun repeating, so the delay is only applied on the first step

0xd186.name: wExpLevelUpFanfare
0xd186.note: [8-bit] $ff when a level-up has just happened; TickLevelUpJingle plays the jingle off it and clears it

scopes.note: The five handlers are reached by `jp hl` out of DrillSubHandlers_1d, so no dataflow proves their bank and only handler 3 is traced. RecordDrillResult runs `wram_bank $06` at its head ($7cc6) and never changes it again, so bank $06 is live throughout -- the range says so where the analysis cannot.

0xd152.name: wPendingExpAwardAmounts
0xd152.note: [10 bytes] Five 16-bit EXP amounts, one per line of the results screen's award list: 0 story, 1 exhibition, 2 linked, 3 match/minigame, 4 trophy. RecordDrillResult takes the line in `b` and dispatches through DrillSubHandlers_1d, each handler storing `de` at this base + 2 * line; ClearDrillResultBuffer zeroes all 15 bytes of the pair. DrawNextExpAwardMessage reads the word back with split-base addressing (`add $52 / adc $d1`) and skips a line whose amount is zero, and HasPendingExpAwards ORs the five words to decide whether the screen is worth showing at all.

0xd15c.name: wPendingExpAwardVariants
0xd15c.note: [5 bytes] One byte per award line, the `c` argument of RecordDrillResult. DrawNextExpAwardMessage adds it to the line's base text id from DrawNextExpAwardMessageTable, so it picks between wordings of the same message -- ShowExpAwardForMatch passes 0, 2, 3 or 4 for a normal, Island Open, practice or Dream match, and the trophy pass numbers the six trophy groups.

0xd151.name: wExpScreenFlags
0xd151.note: [8-bit] Bit flags the EXP award screen runs on: ExpScreenNumberTask sets bit 7 once the EXP-to-next figure has reached zero, ExpScreenDrawTask branches on it each frame, and SignExtendModifierByte rewrites it as it works. Bank $1d keeps the high half of wExpPoolTotal over the same byte, which is why this variant is scoped to bank $1a

unions.comment:
Overworld actor engine scratch (WRAM bank $04), owned by the bank $04
actor-script VM. Scoped to that bank as well as to the WRAM bank: the
VM selects the bank once on entry, so most references cannot prove it.

0xdaea.name: wPlayerMoveAngle
0xdaea.note: [8-bit] Heading the D-pad asks the overworld player to walk in ($40 per quarter turn, matching the FACE_* encoding). UpdatePlayerControl also writes it to actor field +$34, then probes $20/$40/$e0/$c0 away from it to slide along a blocked wall

0xdaec.name: wPlayerMoveAngleApplied
0xdaec.note: [8-bit] Heading actually walked this frame, 0 when the move was blocked

0xdaed.name: wPlayerMoveAnglePrev
0xdaed.note: [8-bit] Previous frame's wPlayerMoveAngleApplied, saved before it is recomputed

0xdaee.name: wPlayerMoving
0xdaee.note: [8-bit] Cleared when no direction is held, so the walk animation stops

0xdaf7.name: wActorScriptBank
0xdaf7.note: [8-bit] ROM bank of the actor script currently executing, taken from the actor's field +$22. Every ActorScriptOp_* passes it to FarReadByte / FarReadWord / CallHLInBankA to reach the script bytes

0xdaf4.name: wActorProbeAngle
0xdaf4.note: [8-bit] Random direction TryPickRandomReachableTarget probes in: the low byte of AdvanceRandomSeed masked with $fc, so one of 64 angles. ProjectPointFromActor casts a ray this way (first at distance $0100, then at $00e0 once the point is confirmed inside the box) to turn the angle into a candidate destination.

0xdaf5.name: wActorRandBoxHalfWidth
0xdaf5.note: [8-bit] Half-width of the box ActorScriptOp_RandBox confines a random target to; the low byte of the operand word it reads with FarReadWord. TryPickRandomReachableTarget passes it to TestPointInBox as h, which is checked against the box centre's first coordinate (b +/- h vs d).

0xdaf6.name: wActorRandBoxHalfDepth
0xdaf6.note: [8-bit] Half-depth of the same box, the high byte of ActorScriptOp_RandBox's operand word. Passed to TestPointInBox as l and checked against the second coordinate (c +/- l vs e); the centre itself is the word at actor + $16.

0xdaef.name: wActorProbeRange
0xdaef.note: [8-bit] How far ahead GetPointAheadOfActorRanged probes: multiplied by 32 (five `add a`) and added to the facing nibble to index ActorMoveVectors_04, so it selects which 32-byte range row of that table the direction vector is read from. The unranged entry point next to it hard-codes $40 instead.

0xdaf0.name: wActorQueryPointX
0xdaf0.note: [16-bit LE] First coordinate of the point FindActorAtPoint is searching at, stashed from hl before it walks wNearbyActorList.

0xdaf2.name: wActorQueryPointY
0xdaf2.note: [16-bit LE] Second coordinate of the same query point, stashed from de. The actor loop reads it back into de for each candidate, comparing against the word at actor + $0e.

unions.comment:
Story-script scratch, second half ($c2b0-$c2bf as a whole is the
current location's scratch block; wMapSceneStage and wMapSceneStage2
are its first two bytes). Two consumers overlay it: bank $14's island
cutscenes keep two sprite slots here as parallel byte arrays, and bank
$15's water-sprite swing contest keeps 16-bit counters over the same
bytes. The three wWaterSpriteMinigame* names that used to sit here in
ram_map.json were global, so they also labelled the generic scratch use
in banks $0e/$0f/$10/$13, which is what STATUS flagged as mis-scoped.
Everywhere else the block is generic per-location scratch, which is what
the default variant names.

0xc2b2.name: wCutsceneObjX
0xc2b2.note: [2 bytes] World X of cutscene sprite slot 0 and slot 1; the drawers subtract hScrollX to get the OAM X. The plane sequence has no second object and borrows slot 0's byte as its frame counter (AdvancePlaneFrameCounter_14)

0xc2b4.name: wCutsceneObjY
0xc2b4.note: [2 bytes] World Y of the two cutscene sprite slots

0xc2b6.name: wCutsceneObjPhase
0xc2b6.note: [2 bytes] Animation phase of each slot: the splash's rise/fall step and the firework's burst step, both used to index the frame tables

0xc2b8.name: wCutsceneObjTimer
0xc2b8.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot frame timer -- the splash's hit counter (0-8) and the firework's countdown to the next burst frame

0xc2ba.name: wCutsceneObjLimit
0xc2ba.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot phase limit, rerolled from the RNG when a splash respawns

0xc2bc.name: wCutsceneObjRiseTimer
0xc2bc.note: [2 bytes] Frames left in the rise, counted down by AdvanceWaterSplash0Rise_14 / AdvanceWaterSplash1Rise_14, which also lift wCutsceneObjY by 2 each frame

0xc2be.name: wCutsceneObjActive
0xc2be.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot active flag; 0 means the object is still rising and the hit test is skipped

0xc2b4.name: wSwingContestTimer
0xc2b4.note: [16-bit] Frames left in the swing contest; WaterSpriteSwingCountTask counts it down and ends the contest at 0

0xc2b6.name: wSwingContestSwings
0xc2b6.note: [16-bit] Swings counted so far, incremented on each A/B press and printed by PrintHexWord as the contest runs

0xc2b8.name: wSwingContestPrevInput
0xc2b8.note: [8-bit] A/B rising edge from the previous frame, so one press counts once

0xc2b9.name: wSwingContestSwingState
0xc2b9.note: [8-bit] 2 once a swing has been registered, 1 on the frame after -- which is how the swing animation is triggered exactly once

0xc2bb.name: wSwingContestHudPage
0xc2bb.note: [8-bit] Which HUD page the swing contest shows; InitWaterSpriteMinigameHud seeds it and QueueWaterSpriteMinigameHudPanels queues the panels for it

0xc2b2.name: wMapScratch
0xc2b2.note: [14 bytes] The rest of the current location's scratch block, after wMapSceneStage / wMapSceneStage2. Every story script in banks $0e-$13 uses it for whatever that location needs -- a saved actor position, a name being assembled for a text argument, a menu's working bytes -- so the block has a name and the offsets do not. The two overlays that do have a fixed layout (bank $14's cutscene sprite slots, bank $15's swing contest) are the scoped variants above

unions.comment:
Screen tilemap buffers, WRAM bank $03. The full-screen UIs assemble their
BG map at $d000 and its CGB attributes at $d400 -- 32 x 32 cells each, rows
TILEMAP_WIDTH apart, of which the top-left 20 x 18 is on screen -- then
QueueVRAMCopy them to $9800 in VRAM banks 0 and 1. Not every screen pairs
the planes this way: the bank $03 cutscenes keep the attribute plane at
$d000 in WRAM bank $02 instead, which is why these names are scoped to a
provable WRAM bank $03 rather than to the addresses.
wShadowTilemapBank / wShadowTilemapPtr point the text engine at whichever
bank the current screen uses ($03 for screens, $05 for text windows, $02 for
the match). Cell addresses render as `base + row * TILEMAP_WIDTH + column`,
which is what they are.

variants.context: character-data / EXP screen cells (mirrored across WRAM banks $02/$03)

0xd000.name: wCharDataScreenCell
0xd000.note: [1024 bytes] The live screen the character-data and EXP screens draw into, one 32 x 32 cell plane in *each* of WRAM banks $02 and $03 -- bank $03 the tile half, bank $02 the CGB attribute half, cell for cell at the same address. Every reference here is an argument to a routine that selects those banks itself (CharDataScreen_WriteStatNumber writes [de] under $03 then $02; ApplyTilemapPatchList and its EXP-screen twin do the same), so the WRAM bank live at the call site is $06 -- the screen's own working set -- and says nothing about the operand. That is why these scopes are ROM ranges with no wram_bank: the callee picks the bank, so the site's is not a constraint to apply. Scoped to the exact call-site ranges rather than whole banks because banks $1c/$1d also address genuine WRAM bank $06 variables in $d2xx-$d3xx.

variants.context: character-data screen backup (mirrored across WRAM banks $02/$03)

0xd430.name: wCharDataScreenBackup
0xd430.note: [576 bytes] Snapshot of the visible screen -- 18 rows of 32 cells, one copy in each of WRAM banks $02 and $03 -- taken once at the top of AnimateCharDataStatsReveal and copied back before every step of the reveal, so each step redraws its bands over the same clean background. The 576 comes from CopyMemoryFast's `c` being a count of 16-byte blocks, not of bytes: `ld c, $24` is 36 blocks. Same size as wCharDataPageSlot1-3, and it lands inside wCharDataPagePlane's extent, but it is a save area rather than page content -- the plane's rows above it ($d400-$d42f) are band 8's staging row and the stat pages patch cells straight through $d430 while this snapshot is not live.

variants.context: character-data screen page plane (mirrored across WRAM banks $02/$03)

0xd400.name: wCharDataPagePlane
0xd400.note:
[992 bytes] Base stat-page rows for the character-data screen, one 31 x 32 cell plane in *each* of WRAM banks $02 and $03: bank $03 holds the tile half, bank $02 the CGB attribute half, cell for cell at the same addresses. LoadBasePageIntoWorkTilemap copies a row from here to the live screen twice, once per bank, which is why the two `ld hl` operands of that pair are the same word. Not an attribute map, despite falling where wShadowAttrmap sits for every other screen; the page slots proper start at wCharDataPageSlot1.
Bank $1c stages the stat-distribution screen's reveal bands in the same rows: BlitTilemapRunsFromTable takes a source base in `bc`, and the eight bands walk $d240, $d280, $d2d0, $d310, $d370, $d3e0 and $d410 -- rows 18 to 32 of one continuous plane, alternating column 0 and column 16 -- so band 8's base is this plane's first row. The 576 bytes from `+ 1 * TILEMAP_WIDTH + 16` on are wCharDataScreenBackup, a save area rather than page content, which is why that address is a variant of its own above.
The three instruction ranges are bank $1d's cell arguments, handed to CharDataScreen_WriteStatNumber and ApplyTilemapPatchList exactly like wCharDataScreenCell's and with the same consequence: WRAM bank $06 is live at the reference, so those scopes name no wram_bank and let the callee pick the plane.

variants.context: screen tilemap (any bank, where WRAM bank $03 is provable)

0xd000.name: wShadowTilemap
0xd000.note:
[1024 bytes] BG tile map the screen is being assembled into, 32 x 32 cells
with rows TILEMAP_WIDTH apart; CopyTilemapRect steps rows by $0020

0xd400.name: wShadowAttrmap
0xd400.note:
[1024 bytes] CGB attribute plane for wShadowTilemap, same geometry $400
higher; SetWinLosePortraitPaletteAttrs writes $d48b for the cell whose
tile byte is $d08b

unions.comment:
Minigame actor records (WRAM bank $04), owned by bank $0d. The bank is
earned from the dispatcher rather than the references: bank $08's
RunMinigamePointLoop and UpdateMatchFrame select bank $04 before
CallModeHook, and ClearMinigameActors / SetMinigameActorHandler /
SetMinigameActorPosition each select it again, but the hooks are reached
through a far pointer so compute_wram_bank cannot follow the edge.
Bank $0a lays a second array over the same bytes with a different record
size: fifteen 14-byte target records where bank $0d has seven 16-byte
actors. Both start with bit 0 of +$00 as the live flag, but the strides
and the field offsets differ (bank $0a's spawn writes its script pointer
at +$04, bank $0d's handler pointer goes to +$0e), so they are two
overlays rather than one structure.

0xdc00.name: wMinigameActors
0xdc00.note:
[112 bytes] Seven 16-byte actor records, cleared as a block by
ClearMinigameActors. Fields, addressed through bc by the helpers:
+$00 flags (bit 0 = enabled, bit 1 = has a handler), +$02 state,
+$03 timer, +$06 world X (16-bit), +$08 world depth (16-bit),
+$0a projected screen X (16-bit), +$0c projected screen Y (16-bit),
+$0e handler pointer.

0xdc70.name: wMinigameSceneActor
0xdc70.note:
[16 bytes] The eighth record, same layout, left out of the
ClearMinigameActors block. It is the object the minigame itself drives --
the shot target, the Boo, the treasure box -- and the only record the
code addresses by literal address rather than through bc, which is why
its fields show up as wMinigameSceneActor + n.

0xdc00.name: wMinigameTargets
0xdc00.note: [210 bytes] Fifteen 14-byte target records for the target-shot minigames. UpdateMinigameTargets walks exactly fifteen of them with `ld de, $000e` between records, and SpawnMinigameTargetsFromList fills them from a formation's script-pointer list with the same stride. Fields, addressed through bc: +$00 flags (bit 0 = live), +$01 the delay ActivateMinigameTarget zeroes, +$04 the target script pointer. UpdateMinigameTarget copies the record it is working on out to wMinigameTargetWork and back. InitMinigameTargets clears with `ld c, $10` through ClearMemory16, i.e. 256 bytes -- past the array's end and over wMinigameTargetWork as well.

unions.comment:
Scrolling text screen (the staff-roll style crawl), WRAM bank $06,
owned by bank $03's RunScrollingTextScreen.
The EXP award screen (bank $1a) overlays the same bytes with its gauge
state, and banks $1c/$1d put the character-data screen's $40-byte stat
blocks at $d240/$d280/$d2d0 -- those stay numeric, being neither.

0xd230.name: wScrollTextDelay
0xd230.note: [8-bit] Frames until the crawl scrolls one line; reloaded with 2 each time it hits 0

0xd231.name: wScrollTextDelayReload
0xd231.note: [8-bit] The value it reloads with, seeded alongside it

0xd232.name: wScrollTextId
0xd232.note: [16-bit] Text id the crawl is rendering, seeded with $1863

0xd234.name: wScrollTextDone
0xd234.note: [8-bit] Set once the last line has scrolled off, which stops the scroll without leaving the loop

0xd230.name: wExpAwardTotal
0xd230.note: [16-bit] EXP being awarded, the target the gauge counts up to

0xd232.name: wExpAwardCounted
0xd232.note: [16-bit] EXP counted so far. AdvanceExpGaugeFill increments it once per tick and sets wExpCountDone when it reaches wExpAwardTotal

0xd234.name: wExpCountedSprite
0xd234.note: [4 bytes] How the counted number is drawn: +$00 X, +$01 Y, +$02 first digit tile ("0"; a digit adds its value * 2), +$03 OAM attribute

0xd238.name: wExpCountDone
0xd238.note: [8-bit] Set once wExpAwardCounted has reached the total; the fill loop leaves and the level-up path runs

0xd239.name: wExpCountFastForward
0xd239.note: [8-bit] Set when the player presses A or B during the count, which switches the gauge to the fast path

0xd23a.name: wExpNumberSpriteShiftX
0xd23a.note: [8-bit] Added to the X of every digit QueueNumberSpritesShifted draws, which is how the counted number slides while the gauge fills

0xd23b.name: wExpLevelUpQueued
0xd23b.note: [8-bit] Latched once the EXP-to-next-level figure reaches zero, so the level-up is requested exactly once

0xd23c.name: wExpToNextLevel
0xd23c.note: [16-bit] EXP still needed for the next level, seeded from GetExpRemainingToNextLevel and counted down alongside the gauge

0xd23e.name: wExpToNextSprite
0xd23e.note: [4 bytes] The same X/Y/tile/attribute record for the EXP-to-next-level number

0xd242.name: wExpToNextDisplayed
0xd242.note: [16-bit] The value actually shown for EXP-to-next; reaching zero is what sets wExpLevelUpQueued

0xd244.name: wExpToNextDigits
0xd244.note: [5 bytes] Decimal digits of wExpToNextDisplayed, formatted unsigned to five places

0xd24e.name: wExpCountedDigits
0xd24e.note: [5 bytes] Decimal digits of wExpAwardCounted, formatted the same way

0xd254.name: wExpAwardSlot
0xd254.note: [8-bit] Which character record the award belongs to, kept so the screen can hand it to AddPlayerExp once the count finishes

unions.comment:
Match object slots (WRAM bank $04): five 16-byte records the bank $09
sprite engine animates along a move curve -- serve indicators, the
court banner, the point-situation banner, special-shot effects.
Scoped to banks $08/$09 as well as the WRAM bank because the spawners
pass a slot base in bc without selecting the bank at the reference.
$ddd0-$ddef above them belongs to the bank $18/$1b menu screens.
Only the bank $08 scope carries wram_bank $04. Bank $08 reaches WRAM bank
$02 as well -- RefreshCourtScoreboard's saved-court-plane addresses were
rendering as object slots until a bank-annotated trace showed the bank --
whereas bank $09 is the object engine itself and never selects another.

0xdd80.name: wObjSlot0
0xdd80.note:
[16 bytes] Match object slot 0. UpdateAllObjSprites walks the five in order; each spawner claims a fixed one (the court banner and the special-shot effect both take slot 3). Object-slot record, 16 bytes:
  +$00 object id, $ff = slot free (ProcessObjSlot skips it)
  +$01 flags; bit 0 = draw this frame
  +$02 sprite template pointer, passed to QueueSpriteTemplate as hl
  +$04 OAM attribute (b), +$05 base tile (c)
  +$06 X offset, +$07 Y offset
  +$08 handler pointer -- ProcessObjSlot `jp`s to it with DrawObjSlot
       pushed as the return address
  +$0a X from the move curve, +$0b Y
  +$0c handler sub-state, an RST00 index the handler steps
  +$0d curve step, incremented every frame by FinishObjSlotUpdate
  +$0e curve id, indexing MoveCurveTable_09
  +$0f anchor: 0 draws at the offsets as they stand, 1 adds the serving
       character's wCharScreenX/Y first

0xdd90.name: wObjSlot1
0xdd90.note:
[16 bytes] Match object slot 1. UpdateAllObjSprites walks the five in order; each spawner claims a fixed one (the court banner and the special-shot effect both take slot 3). Object-slot record, 16 bytes:
  +$00 object id, $ff = slot free (ProcessObjSlot skips it)
  +$01 flags; bit 0 = draw this frame
  +$02 sprite template pointer, passed to QueueSpriteTemplate as hl
  +$04 OAM attribute (b), +$05 base tile (c)
  +$06 X offset, +$07 Y offset
  +$08 handler pointer -- ProcessObjSlot `jp`s to it with DrawObjSlot
